p2_b4.ocr: The control group exhibited a baseline total cell count of 6.00 ± 2.35, which serves as a reference point for comparison against the experimental conditions. Notably, the addition of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) resulted in a substantial increase in total cells, reaching 80.60 ± 16.30**, an indication of the heightened cellular activity triggered by this treatment.

p2_b5.ocr: Conversely, the conditions labeled C + LPS + I and C + LPS + N demonstrated resultant changes of 36.20 ± 7.26## and 43.40 ± 6.91##, respectively, suggesting varying degrees of cellular response contingent upon the specific treatment combinations. This data underlines the significance of integrating advanced techniques, such as Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy (IMRT), into clinical practice for conditions like prostate, breast, and head and neck cancers. The findings advocate for earlier incorporation of IMRT technique training within planning units to enhance practical experience and improve patient outcomes.
